tagline: Mahachai, the port town on the Gulf with a huge fish market, salt flats, and fresh seafood
introHtml:
Samut Sakhon sits just south of Bangkok, and locals call it Mahachai. It is one of the country's biggest fishing and fish-landing towns, where shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish come in from the Gulf every day and ship out across Thailand. The town has the busy Mahachai market that fills up from early morning, with the Mae Klong railway line running right through the middle of it, which has become the image people remember.

Outside town toward Ban Laem and Khok Kham, salt flats and mangrove forest stretch as far as you can see. It is a short drive from Bangkok, so people come to eat seafood by the water, stop to watch the salt flats in the late afternoon, then buy seafood to take home.
bestTime: November–February, cool and dry, easy weather for walking the markets and seeing the salt flats

highlights.name: Mahachai and the Talay Thai market
highlights.blurb: The town's central district, a fish-landing port and large seafood market with fresh shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish daily. Good for buying seafood and grabbing breakfast.

highlights.name: Mahachai market and the Mae Klong railway
highlights.blurb: An old market in the town center with the Mahachai railway line running through it, shoppers mingling with the tracks. It is part of everyday life here.

highlights.name: Ban Laem–Khok Kham salt flats
highlights.blurb: Sea-salt flats lined up along the coastal road. In the late afternoon the light reflects off the water beautifully. This is one of the province's oldest salt-making areas.

highlights.name: Tha Chalom
highlights.blurb: An old community across the river from town, reachable by ferry from Mahachai. It has old shophouses, Chinese shrines, and was Thailand's first sanitary district.

highlights.name: Don Hoi Lot (the side near Ban Laem)
highlights.blurb: A sandy-muddy bar along the Gulf where razor clams live in the mud. People come to walk the shore and eat seafood by the water.

highlights.name: Mangrove forest and shorebirds
highlights.blurb: The mangroves around Khok Kham and Ban Laem are home to shorebirds. In winter many migratory birds come through to watch.

foodScene.name: Mahachai seafood
foodScene.note: The province's best-known food. Restaurants by the water and in town have fresh shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish daily because they sit right by the fish-landing port.

foodScene.name: Mae Klong mackerel–fresh pla thu
foodScene.note: The pla thu (short mackerel) from the Gulf around here is plump. Steamed or fried with chili dip, it is a local staple and a popular take-home gift.

foodScene.name: Cockles–blanched shellfish
foodScene.note: Plump cockles from the Gulf, blanched and dipped in seafood sauce. You can find them at seafood spots and fresh markets.

foodScene.name: Shrimp and sea crab
foodScene.note: The Mahachai fish port lands sea shrimp, blue crab, and mud crab every day. Seafood restaurants grill, steam, and cook them fresh.

foodScene.name: Processed seafood and shrimp paste
foodScene.note: Being a fishing town, it makes shrimp paste, fish sauce, salted fish, and dried seafood for sale, popular gifts that people stop to buy.

foodScene.name: Noodles and street food in Mahachai market
foodScene.note: The central market has noodles, rice-and-curry stalls, and snacks to try. It is where locals come to eat.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and grill restaurants
foodScene.note: There are plenty of mu kratha (DIY barbecue) spots around the neighborhoods and villages, a go-to dinner for friends and families.

foodScene.name: Isan food and som tam
foodScene.note: The factory areas and markets have lots of som tam, grilled chicken, and laap, since many Isan workers have moved here and opened shops.

attractions.name: Talay Thai market and Mahachai fish port
attractions.blurb: A large seafood market next to the fishing pier with fresh seafood landing daily. Good for browsing and buying to take home.

attractions.name: Mahachai market and the Mae Klong railway
attractions.blurb: An old market in the town center with a train running through it, shoppers mingling with the tracks. It is part of everyday life here.

attractions.name: Ban Laem–Khok Kham salt flats
attractions.blurb: Sea-salt flats lined up along the coast. In the late afternoon the light reflects off the water beautifully. An old salt-making area.

attractions.name: Tha Chalom
attractions.blurb: An old riverside community across from town, reachable by ferry. It has old shophouses, Chinese shrines, and was Thailand's first sanitary district.

attractions.name: Wat Chong Lom
attractions.blurb: An old temple on the Tha Chin River in Mahachai, a temple tied to the town where people stop to pay respects and see the murals.

attractions.name: Phan Thai Norasing Shrine
attractions.blurb: The shrine and memorial to Phan Thai Norasing beside Khok Kham canal, telling an old story from the Ayutthaya era.

attractions.name: Khok Kham mangrove forest
attractions.blurb: A stretch of mangrove forest and a nature boardwalk along the Gulf. In winter migratory shorebirds come through to watch.

attractions.name: Don Hoi Lot (the side near Ban Laem)
attractions.blurb: A sandy-muddy bar along the Gulf with razor clams in the mud. You can walk the shore and eat seafood by the water.

itineraryIdeas: Samut Sakhon 1 day — Mahachai, Tha Chalom, and seafood
Samut Sakhon for seafood lovers — Talay Thai market and waterfront restaurants
Samut Sakhon for nature — salt flats and Khok Kham mangroves
Samut Sakhon for markets — Mahachai market and the railway
